extraFacts.fact: Unit conversions (1 bar = 14.5038 psi): 100 psi = about 7 bar; 120 psi = about 8 bar; 125 psi = about 9 bar; 140 psi = about 10 bar; 145 psi = 10 bar; 150 psi = about 10 bar; 200 psi = about 14 bar; 246 psi = about 17 bar; 250 psi = about 17 bar; 300 psi = about 21 bar; 350 psi = about 24 bar; 500 psi = about 34 bar. Temperature (°C = (°F - 32) / 1.8): -40°F = -40°C; -32°F = -36°C; -25°F = -32°C; -10°F = -23°C; -4°F = -20°C; 0°F = -18°C; 15°F = -9°C; 23°F = -5°C; 32°F = 0°C; 122°F = 50°C; 140°F = 60°C; 150°F = 66°C; 158°F = 70°C; 160°F = 71°C; 176°F = 80°C; 200°F = 93°C; 350°F = 177°C; 400°F = 204°C; 450°F = 232°C.
extraFacts.source: NIST SP 811 unit conversion; 1 bar = 14.5038 psi

extraFacts.fact: NPT is the American taper pipe thread to ASME B1.20.1 and NPTF is the dryseal version to ASME B1.20.3; BSPP (G) is parallel pipe thread to ISO 228-1 and BSPT (R) is taper pipe thread to ISO 7-1. NPT and BSP threads do not mate. FNPT is female NPT and MNPT is male NPT.
extraFacts.source: ASME B1.20.1; ASME B1.20.3; ISO 228-1; ISO 7-1

extraFacts.fact: HS 2022 heading 84.81 covers taps, cocks and valves: subheading 8481.20 valves for oleohydraulic or pneumatic transmissions, 8481.30 check (non-return) valves, 8481.40 safety or relief valves, 8481.80 other appliances. The importing country's tariff fixes the final national digits.
ISO 4414 sets the general rules and safety requirements for pneumatic fluid power systems, including that stored pressure be able to be isolated and exhausted before work on the machine.
extraFacts.source: ISO 4414:2010 Pneumatic fluid power - General rules and safety requirements for systems and their components

extraFacts.fact: Pressure vessel rules require a safety (pop) valve to be set at or below the maximum allowable working pressure of the vessel or system it protects, and its flow capacity to be at least the maximum the compressor can deliver. Set pressure is chosen by the user from the preset values offered.
extraFacts.source: ASME Boiler and Pressure Vessel Code Section VIII Division 1, paragraph UG-134 (pressure setting of pressure relief devices) and UG-125

extraFacts.fact: In a soft seat safety valve a resilient seat seals against a metal disc so the valve reseats tight close to its set pressure; in a hard seat (metal-to-metal) valve both parts are metal, which tolerates higher temperature. Conrader part numbers carry the set pressure in psi as the last field, and the SRV and SRH prefixes mark soft seat and hard seat.
extraFacts.source: Conrader SRV (soft seat) and SRH (hard seat) safety valve part numbers in Indus size tables; Kingston soft and hard seat pop valve descriptions

extraFacts.fact: A soft start valve pressurises the downstream line slowly and then opens fully; a dump valve exhausts the downstream line when its signal is removed; a combined soft start/dump valve does both and is fitted ahead of the equipment. Parker Global modular soft start and dump valves are available with solenoid or external or internal air pilot operators. A lockout valve shuts the supply and vents the downstream air and can be locked off with a padlock so the machine cannot be re-pressurised during maintenance.
extraFacts.source: Parker Hannifin Global air preparation catalogue (soft start, dump and lockout valves); ISO 4414:2010
